name: TitanFuzz
one_liner: Evolutionary fuzzing of deep-learning libraries (PyTorch and TensorFlow) using infill language models as structure-aware AST mutation operators.

loop.proposes: A generative model (Codex) seeds multi-API tensor programs, and an infill model (InCoder) masks and regenerates spans around selected AST operators.
loop.judged_by: PyTorch and TensorFlow CPU/GPU execution engines, differential backends, and crash/NaN sanitizers evaluate every mutated program and log operator coverage.
loop.steers: An evolutionary fitness function combining API depth, dataflow graph edges, and new branch coverage selects seeds for the next mutation round.

headline_result: Achieved 50.84% (PyTorch) and 30.38% (TensorFlow) higher code coverage than state-of-the-art DL fuzzers and detected 65 bugs (41 confirmed previously unknown).
caveat: Differential testing across CPU and GPU backends can trigger false-positive floating-point rounding discrepancies if tolerances are too tight.
beyond_harness_note: An evolutionary coverage-guided fuzzing loop manages the seed corpus and invokes the infill LLM as a span-mutation operator.
generative_model: Codex seed generator + InCoder span mutator
algorithmic_authority: Dataflow/branch coverage analyzer and differential execution oracle

sources.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Fuzzers: Fuzzing Deep-Learning Libraries via Large Language Models (ISSTA 2023 / arXiv:2212.14834)

verification.notes: Re-checked against Deng, Xia, Peng, Yang and Zhang, arXiv:2212.14834 (abstract, comment "Accepted at ISSTA 2023"). Corrections: card previously cited unrelated arXiv:2212.14836; the coverage figures were attached to the wrong libraries (paper: 30.38% TensorFlow, 50.84% PyTorch) and are code coverage, not API coverage. Codex generator and InCoder infill model confirmed. Fitness-function and differential-oracle details were not re-read in the paper body.
